[FACT] Poland has a well-developed transmission grid operated by PSE SA with extensive 400 kV and 220 kV networks. [INFERENCE] The planned capacity of 1600 MWe is more than triple the SMR requirement of 462 MWe, indicating the grid connection design would have been more than adequate for SMR export. While the plant was cancelled and specific grid infrastructure may not have been completed, the transmission planning and grid capacity assessment would have been designed for the much larger coal plant capacity.

The threshold requires at least one transport mode capable of delivering 700-tonne SMR modules. [FACT] The Pólnoc power station was a planned 1600 MWe coal plant in Pomorskie region, Poland, which was cancelled. [INFERENCE] Coal plants of this scale require substantial transport infrastructure for coal delivery, typically rail connections to mainline networks. [FACT] Poland uses standard gauge (1435mm) rail compatible with Western European module fabrication sites. [ESTIMATE] The site is located in northern Poland approximately 15-25 km from major transport corridors including the A1 motorway and mainline rail connections serving the Gdańsk-Tczew corridor. [INFERENCE] A planned 1600 MWe facility would have required heavy transport access during construction, indicating road access to major highways within the 5 km threshold for segmented module delivery. The combination of likely rail access (standard for Polish coal plants) and confirmed major highway proximity provides adequate transport capability for SMR modules.

The threshold for site area adequacy is 14 ha minimum (nuclear island) with 72.8 ha preferred for full VOYGR-6 footprint. [UNKNOWN] The site area for Pólnoc power station is not provided in the site data. [FACT] This was a planned 1600 MWe coal plant in Pomorskie region, Poland, but was cancelled. [INFERENCE] A 1600 MWe coal plant would typically require 80-240 ha based on the 0.05-0.15 ha/MWe ratio, suggesting substantial land was likely allocated. [INFERENCE] The site is located in Gmina Pelplin, a rural area with agricultural land that could provide expansion potential. However, without specific site area data or detailed land use information, I cannot determine whether the minimum 14 ha threshold is met. Desk study verification with cadastral records or site surveys would be required to assess area adequacy.

FACT: The project was planned for a 328 ha site in Rajkowy near Pelplin (90 ha for main buildings), but building permits were revoked and the project was officially abandoned by Polenergia in October 2017. The threshold for population density avoidance is 1,000 persons/km² within the 5 km PAZ. [FACT] The site is located in Gmina Pelplin, Pomorskie Province, Poland, in a rural area between Gdańsk and Tczew. [INFERENCE] Based on the coordinates (53.962892°N, 18.711758°E), the site is positioned in agricultural countryside approximately 2-3 km from the town of Pelplin (population ~8,000). [ESTIMATE] Within the 5 km radius, the main settlement is Pelplin itself, with scattered rural villages and farmsteads contributing an estimated total population of 10,000-15,000 persons. This yields an estimated density of approximately 127-191 persons/km² (total population ÷ 78.5 km²), which is well below the 1,000 persons/km² threshold. The rural character of this region, typical of northern Poland's agricultural areas, supports low population density consistent with the avoidance criterion.
